Re: Appeal of denial for lumbar decompression/discectomy  
Member: Skyler Jennings  
Member ID: W298663271  
Reference number: POC-E84DB56372-39024  
Requested procedure: CPT 63030  
Denial date: August 17, 2026  

Dear HealthPartners Appeals Reviewer:

I appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030, lumbar laminotomy/discectomy with decompression of the affected nerve root. The denial states that the submitted imaging does not support medical necessity. The clinical and imaging records directly address the imaging issue and establish that the requested procedure is medically necessary.

The submitted MRI, performed on June 25, 2026, shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing right L5 nerve root. The imaging abnormality corresponds to the patient’s clinical findings: radicular pain into the right calf, inability to stand for more than 10 minutes, positive provocative testing on the affected side, and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level.

The patient has had progressive lower-back pain for 14 months, unrelieved by rest. Symptoms have continued despite extensive conservative treatment, including:

- Supervised physical therapy focused on core stabilization and lumbar flexibility for 12 weeks, from March 28, 2026, through June 20, 2026;
- Twenty completed physical therapy visits, documented in the physical therapy discharge note;
- NSAID treatment for eight months with inadequate relief; and
- A corticosteroid injection on April 30, 2026, producing only two weeks of partial relief.

The public HealthPartners document titled Spinal decompression surgeries contains the following criteria:

“Clinical documentation indicates presence/diagnosis of a condition or conditions causing spinal cord and/or nerve root compression.”

“Clinical documentation indicates presence of at least one sign/symptom, associated with the condition(s), limiting activities of daily living.”

“Clinical documentation includes radiographic results (e.g., plain radiographs, advanced imaging studies), confirming the presence of spinal cord and/or nerve root compression caused by the condition(s) and supporting the indication for the decompression surgery.”

“Clinical documentation shows the sign(s)/symptom(s), identified in criterion 2 above, persist despite completion of at least 8 weeks of intensive conservative treatments.”

The records satisfy each of those quoted criteria:

1. The L4-L5 disc extrusion and severe right lateral recess stenosis are documented conditions causing compression of the traversing right L5 nerve root.

2. The patient has persistent radicular pain into the right calf, a corresponding neurologic deficit, and severe standing intolerance limited to approximately 10 minutes. These symptoms substantially restrict daily activities.

3. The June 25, 2026 MRI confirms the disc extrusion, severe lateral recess stenosis, and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. The imaging findings are at the same level and on the same side as the patient’s symptoms and examination findings.

4. Symptoms have persisted for 14 months despite more than eight weeks of conservative treatment. The patient completed 20 supervised physical therapy visits over 12 weeks, used NSAIDs for eight months without adequate relief, and obtained only temporary partial relief from a corticosteroid injection.

The patient’s clinical findings are therefore not merely nonspecific back pain. They demonstrate persistent, function-limiting right L5 radiculopathy caused by a specific compressive lesion identified on MRI. CPT 63030 is requested to decompress the affected nerve root at the documented L4-L5 level.

Please overturn the denial and approve CPT 63030. If HealthPartners maintains the denial, please provide the exact medical-necessity criteria and guideline version applied to this request, including any Cohere Health, InterQual, MCG, or other third-party criteria; identify the specific imaging requirement that HealthPartners believes was not met; and explain why the June 25, 2026 MRI does not establish the documented nerve-root compression.

The public HealthPartners document quoted above has not been confirmed as the governing policy for this Commercial/ACA plan. The denial letter does not identify the policy, policy number, guideline version, or effective date used in this determination. Please include that information with the appeal decision.

Please consider the enclosed clinical records, including the MRI report, physical therapy discharge note, medication history, injection record, and examination findings. I request a full and fair review by a reviewer who was not involved in the original determination.

Sincerely,

Skyler Jennings
